about: The code↔view boundary (#1879). "enforced": every reach across the boundary that exists today, exact per file — one more is a failure, one fewer is stale. "declared": files that convert between code and views in ways no structural rule can see; named and counted, not enforced. Because nothing can see them, the declared list is kept by reading code, so a miss is expected: when one is found, it joins with an "added" line. Both lists only shrink: each new enforced reach needs its own line, "added": { "<reach>": "#<issue> <why>" }, and a newly declared file needs "added": "#<issue> <why>". "krillReaders" (#1972): the files outside codeView/strudelMini/ that still read a field of krill's nodes, by top-level function, with exactly how many reads each makes — one more is a failure, one fewer is stale, and a number never goes up without an "added" line for that function. See boundary.ts.

enforced.why: Runs our reader on every evaluate (StrudelEngine.ts:1651) and stamps irNodeId on each hap from its index (:1620, :2524, :2611, and onTrigger via HapStream.ts:135). Breakpoints, the gutter and the IR inspector read that stamp. The id is a hash of the hap's own span, so the engine can compute it without our IR.

The engine reads the document to decide which track a bare statement's pattern belongs to: chunk detection, plus the track numbering in codeView/mixer/stripModel that the mixer joins on. It sits in the engine's runtime import graph, where importing the entry loads the mini-notation parser ahead of the engine test's mock and the suite dies at load.

added.codeView/mixer/stripModel#bareCaptureIdF: #1882 the engine already imported this file; it moved into the area in #1884, so the same dependency now crosses the boundary
added.codeView/mixer/stripModel#isTrackChunk: #1882 the engine already imported this file; it moved into the area in #1884, so the same dependency now crosses the boundary

enforced.why: A line scanner needs one rule, LABEL_HEAD, and the file that owns it, codeView/ir/trackId.ts, imports nothing (a test keeps it that way). Reaching that leaf adds one dependency-free file to the engine's import graph; the entry would add 44 more codeView modules for one regex (measured 2026-10-04: the engine's graph holds 18 codeView files, the entry's holds 62). A one-rule import from a codeView file that imports nothing is meant to stay (#1880).

added.codeView/ir/trackId#LABEL_HEAD: #1921 the scanner's own copy of the identifier regex became the shared LABEL_HEAD; the entry route broke StrudelEngine.test's collection, so it reads the leaf

enforced.why: A line scanner needs two rules, LABEL_HEAD and TEMPO_SETTERS, and the files that own them, codeView/ir/trackId.ts and codeView/ir/statementHeads.ts, import nothing (a test keeps each that way). Reaching those leaves adds two dependency-free files to the engine's import graph; the entry would add dozens more codeView modules for two names (measured 2026-10-04: the engine's graph holds 18 codeView files, the entry's holds 62). A one-rule import from a codeView file that imports nothing is meant to stay (#1880).

added.codeView/ir/trackId#LABEL_HEAD: #1921 the scanner's own copy of the identifier regex became the shared LABEL_HEAD; the entry route broke StrudelEngine.test's collection, so it reads the leaf
added.codeView/ir/statementHeads#TEMPO_SETTERS: #1927 a tempo setter line ends a block, and the scanner knew only setcps of the four names; it now reads the shared list from codeView/ir/statementHeads.ts, which imports nothing (a test keeps it that way)

krillReaders.why: The old syntactic reader: it works out steps, slots, chords, ops and alternations from krill's tree by hand. It is the code #1012 exists to delete, so it is not rewritten onto the adapter's nodes. Everything else in this file (the span readers, the projections) asks codeView/strudelMini/.
